skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through inference.sh. Configure duration, frame rate, resolution, codec, props, and composition IDs.
skill.summary: Render Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through inference.sh.
skill.author: inference-sh-7

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby shell backtick findings are Markdown false positives, not executable Ruby code. The install command pipes a remote script into sh, which is a confirmed critical supply-chain risk. The skill also sends user TSX code and props to an external rendering service, so stronger install and privacy guidance is needed.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl pipe with a download, checksum verification, and explicit execution steps. Prefer signed packages or pinned release artifacts.

remediation.issue: Render code and props are submitted to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear disclosure that TSX, props, and referenced assets leave the local environment. Warn users not to include secrets.

remediation.issue: Installer trust depends on mutable remote endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Pin CLI versions, publish checksums beside each release, and document how users can verify the binary before login.

content.value_statement: Video teams need a repeatable way to turn React animations into files. This skill renders Remotion TSX through inference.sh and returns MP4 output.
actual_capabilities: Renders React and Remotion TSX components through inference.sh.
Returns MP4 video output from supplied component code.
Accepts duration, frame rate, width, height, codec, props, and composition ID.
Supports Remotion APIs such as spring, interpolate, Sequence, Audio, Video, and Img.
Shows CLI and Python SDK workflows, including streaming render progress.
limitations: Requires inference.sh access and login for CLI examples.
Sends render code, props, and referenced assets to an external service.
Does not document local Remotion rendering or self-hosted execution.
Dependency support depends on the remote rendering environment.

use_cases.title: Produce Branded Motion Clips
use_cases.description: Create short MP4 videos from Remotion components with configured duration, resolution, and frame rate.

use_cases.title: Render Data-Driven Variants
use_cases.description: Pass props into a Remotion component to generate repeated videos for dashboards, reports, or product updates.

use_cases.title: Automate Video Production
use_cases.description: Use CLI or Python SDK examples to render videos and stream progress during longer jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Simple Intro
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a short title animation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three second Remotion title video with a fade-in effect. Render it as MP4 at 1920 by 1080 and 30 fps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Square Social Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with format and motion requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a five second square Remotion video for a social post. Use animated text, brand colors, and 60 fps output.

prompt_templates.title: Render with Dynamic Props
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for reusable component inputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Render this Remotion component with props for title, subtitle, metric, and theme. Return the MP4 output and summarize the settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production workflow for many videos.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CLI or Python SDK workflow that renders multiple Remotion variants and streams progress for each job.

output_examples.input: A request for a two second fade-in title video at 1080p.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an MP4 video link with the selected duration, frame rate, width, and height.

output_examples.input: A square animated counter video for a social media post.
output_examples.output: The skill renders a square MP4 and reports progress while the remote job runs.

output_examples.input: A reusable Remotion component with title and subtitle props.
output_examples.output: The skill renders the component with supplied props and returns the final video output.

best_practices: Keep Remotion components small and deterministic before sending them to the renderer.
Set duration, frame rate, width, and height explicitly for predictable output.
Remove secrets and private assets from code or props before remote rendering.
anti_patterns: Do not paste credentials, tokens, or private customer data into render props.
Do not rely on remote assets that may disappear before rendering finishes.
Do not run remote install scripts without independent verification.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 videos through inference.sh.

faq.question: Can I set video dimensions?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports width, height, frame rate, duration, codec, props, and composition ID settings.

faq.question: Does it support common Remotion APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation lists APIs such as useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, interpolate, AbsoluteFill, and Sequence.

faq.question: Is local rendering included?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow renders through inference.sh rather than a local Remotion project.

faq.question: What should I avoid sending?
faq.answer: Avoid sending secrets, credentials, private customer data, or proprietary assets that should not leave your environment.

faq.question: Can it show render progress?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python SDK example shows streaming updates for render progress and final video output.
